title: Represent time, source coverage, and explicit negative evidence scopes
summary: Build temporal and coverage primitives for historical assessment and missing-event rules. Failed collection and incomplete coverage must remain visible so the system cannot confuse no observation with verified absence.
implementation: Validate explicit time fields without substituting ingestion for unknown event time.
Represent source/query coverage by source set, interval, snapshot/catalog revision, completeness, and failure reasons.
Register negative scopes using typed predicates, knowledge boundaries, and expiry.
Permit retirement only under a declared complete replacement scope; retain prior state on failed or partial empty input.

acceptance.criterion: Late-discovered evidence is excluded from earlier knowledge views while retaining past effective time.
acceptance.verification: Query one corpus at two availability boundaries.

acceptance.criterion: Incomplete empty sources cannot establish absence or retire facts.
acceptance.verification: Compare complete, partial, failed, and not-yet-expected snapshots.

acceptance.criterion: New eligible evidence matches a negative watch despite having an unknown original ID.
acceptance.verification: Insert matching and unrelated records and inspect change signals.

tests: Late cancellation revises current understanding without rewriting yesterday.
Clock progression does not invent an event.
Unrelated arrivals do not invalidate narrow absence scopes.
Incremental silence leaves the matter unresolved.
risks: Treating complete-snapshot omission as universal deletion would corrupt live-stream lifecycle.

reuse.application: Retain retirement only where complete-scope assumptions are explicitly established.
